title.raw: 卷十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 11 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts 1

sentences.zh: 宋孝穆趙皇后 孝懿蕭皇后 武敬臧皇后 武張夫人 文章胡太后 少帝司馬皇后 文元袁皇后 孝武昭路太后 明宣沈太后 孝武文穆王皇后 前廢帝何皇后 明恭王皇后 後廢帝陳太妃 後廢帝江皇后 順陳太妃 順謝皇后 齊宣孝陳皇后 高昭劉皇后 武穆裴皇后 文安王皇后 郁林王何妃 海陵王王妃 明敬劉皇后 東昏褚皇后 和王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiaomu Zhao of Song, Empress Xiaoyi Xiao of Song, Empress Wujing Zang of Song, Lady Zhang of Song Wu, Empress Dowager Wenzhang Hu of Song, Empress Sima of the Lesser Emperor of Song, Empress Wenyuan Yuan of Song, Empress Dowager Zhaowu Lu of Song Xiaowu, Empress Dowager Mingxuan Shen of Song, Empress Wenmu Wang of Song Xiaowu, Empress He of the Former Deposed Emperor of Song, Empress Minggong Wang of Song, Grand Consort Chen of the Later Deposed Emperor of Song, Empress Jiang of the Later Deposed Emperor of Song, Grand Consort Chen of Emperor Shun of Song, Empress Xie of Emperor Shun of Song, Empress Xuanxiao Chen of Qi, Empress Gaozhao Liu of Qi, Empress Wumu Pei of Qi, Empress Wen'an Wang of Qi, Consort He of Prince Yulin of Qi, Consort Wang of Prince Hailing of Qi, Empress Mingjing Liu of Qi, Empress Donghun Chu of Qi, Empress Wang of Prince He of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter treats Empress Xiaomu Zhao of Song, Empress Xiaoyi Xiao, Empress Wujing Zang, Lady Zhang of Emperor Wu of Song, Empress Dowager Wenzhang Hu, Empress Sima of the lesser emperor, Empress Wenyuan Yuan, Empress Dowager Zhaowu Lu of Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Dowager Mingxuan Shen, Empress Wenmu Wang of Emperor Xiaowu, Empress He of the former deposed emperor, Empress Minggong Wang, Grand Consort Chen of the later deposed emperor, Empress Jiang of the later deposed emperor, Grand Consort Chen of Emperor Shun, Empress Xie of Emperor Shun, Empress Xuanxiao Chen of Qi, Empress Gaozhao Liu, Empress Wumu Pei, Empress Wen'an Wang, Consort He of Prince Yulin, Consort Wang of Prince Hailing, Empress Mingjing Liu, Empress Donghun Chu, and Empress Wang of Prince He.

sentences.zh: 六宮位號，前史代有不同。

translations.literal: The ranks and titles of the Six Palaces have differed from one historical record to the next.
translations.idiomatic: The ranks and titles of the inner palace have varied from dynasty to dynasty in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝采漢魏之制，置貴嬪、夫人、貴人，是為三夫人，位視三公；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin adopted the institutions of Han and Wei, establishing Noble Consort, Lady, and Noble Lady as the Three Ladies, their rank equivalent to the Three Dukes;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin took over the Han and Wei systems and created Noble Consort, Lady, and Noble Lady as the Three Ladies, each ranked on a par with the Three Dukes;

sentences.zh: 淑妃、淑媛、淑儀、修華、修容、修儀、婕妤、容華、充華，是為九嬪，位視九卿；

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort, Virtuous Lady of Honor, Virtuous Lady of Elegance, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Beauty, Cultivated Elegance, Fair Lady, Radiant Splendor, and Full Splendor as the Nine Consorts, their rank equivalent to the Nine Ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort, Virtuous Lady of Honor, Virtuous Lady of Elegance, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Beauty, Cultivated Elegance, Fair Lady, Radiant Splendor, and Full Splendor as the Nine Consorts, each ranked on a par with the Nine Ministers;

sentences.zh: 其餘有美人、才人、中才人，爵視千石以下。

translations.literal: Besides these there were Beauty, Talented Lady, and Central Talented Lady, their titles equivalent to officials below the thousand-dan rank.
translations.idiomatic: Below them stood Beauty, Talented Lady, and Central Talented Lady, titles equated with offices beneath the thousand-dan grade.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝省二才人，其餘仍用晉制。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song eliminated the two Talented Lady posts; the rest still followed the Jin system.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song abolished the two Talented Lady posts but otherwise kept the Jin arrangement.

sentences.zh: 案貴嬪，魏文帝所制。

translations.literal: Note: Noble Consort was instituted by Emperor Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort was first created by Emperor Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 夫人，魏武初建魏國所制。

translations.literal: Lady was instituted when Emperor Wu of Wei first established the state of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady was created when Cao Cao first founded the state of Wei.

sentences.zh: 貴人，漢光武所制。

translations.literal: Noble Lady was instituted by Emperor Guangwu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Lady was first created by Emperor Guangwu of Han.

sentences.zh: 淑妃，魏明帝所制。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort was instituted by Emperor Ming of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort was first created by Emperor Ming of Wei.

sentences.zh: 淑媛，魏文帝所制。

translations.literal: Virtuous Lady of Honor was instituted by Emperor Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Lady of Honor was first created by Emperor Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 淑儀、修華，晉武帝所制。

translations.literal: Virtuous Lady of Elegance and Cultivated Splendor were instituted by Emperor Wu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Lady of Elegance and Cultivated Splendor were both creations of Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 修容，魏文帝所制。

translations.literal: Cultivated Beauty was instituted by Emperor Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivated Beauty was first created by Emperor Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 修儀，魏明帝所制。

translations.literal: Cultivated Elegance was instituted by Emperor Ming of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivated Elegance was first created by Emperor Ming of Wei.

sentences.zh: 婕妤、容華，前漢舊號。

translations.literal: Fair Lady and Radiant Splendor are titles from the Former Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fair Lady and Radiant Splendor were titles inherited from the Former Han.

sentences.zh: 充華，晉武帝所制。

translations.literal: Full Splendor was instituted by Emperor Wu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Full Splendor was first created by Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 美人，漢光武所制。

translations.literal: Beauty was instituted by Emperor Guangwu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Beauty was first created by Emperor Guangwu of Han.

sentences.zh: 及孝武孝建三年，省夫人；

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu in the third year of Xiaojian abolished the Lady rank;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the Lady rank was abolished;

sentences.zh: 置貴妃，位比相國，進貴嬪比丞相，貴人比三司，以為三夫人，又置昭儀、昭容、昭華，以代修華、修儀、修容。

translations.literal: He established Noble Consort, rank matching the Chancellor of State; promoted Noble Consort to match the Chancellor; Noble Lady to match the Three Excellencies as the Three Ladies; and also established Bright Elegance, Bright Beauty, and Bright Splendor to replace Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, and Cultivated Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He created Noble Consort with rank equal to the chancellor of state, elevated Noble Consort to match the chancellor, and Noble Lady to match the Three Excellencies as the Three Ladies; he also added Bright Elegance, Bright Beauty, and Bright Splendor in place of Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, and Cultivated Beauty.

sentences.zh: 又置中才人、充衣，以為散位。

translations.literal: He also established Central Talented Lady and Attendant of Full Garments as honorific posts without fixed duties.
translations.idiomatic: He further added Central Talented Lady and Attendant of Full Garments as supernumerary offices.

sentences.zh: 案昭儀，漢元帝所制。

translations.literal: Note: Bright Elegance was instituted by Emperor Yuan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Elegance was first created by Emperor Yuan of Han.

sentences.zh: 昭容，孝武所制。

translations.literal: Bright Beauty was instituted by Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Beauty was first created by Emperor Xiaowu of Song.

sentences.zh: 昭華，魏明帝所制。

translations.literal: Bright Splendor was instituted by Emperor Ming of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Splendor was first created by Emperor Ming of Wei.

sentences.zh: 中才人，晉武帝所制。

translations.literal: Central Talented Lady was instituted by Emperor Wu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Central Talented Lady was first created by Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 充衣，前漢舊制。

translations.literal: Attendant of Full Garments is an old Former Han institution.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant of Full Garments was an old title from the Former Han.

sentences.zh: 及明帝泰始二年，省淑妃、昭華、中才人、充衣，復置修華、修儀、修容、才人、良人；

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming in the second year of Taishi abolished Virtuous Consort, Bright Splendor, Central Talented Lady, and Attendant of Full Garments, and restored Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, Cultivated Beauty, Talented Lady, and Good Woman;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, Virtuous Consort, Bright Splendor, Central Talented Lady, and Attendant of Full Garments were abolished, and Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, Cultivated Beauty, Talented Lady, and Good Woman were restored;

sentences.zh: 三年，又省貴人，置貴姬，以備三夫人之數；

translations.literal: In the third year he again abolished Noble Lady and established Noble Concubine to fill the quota of the Three Ladies;
translations.idiomatic: The next year Noble Lady was abolished and Noble Concubine was created to complete the Three Ladies;

sentences.zh: 又置昭華，增淑容、承徽、列榮；

translations.literal: He also established Bright Splendor, and added Virtuous Beauty, Bearing Emblem, and Arrayed Glory;
translations.idiomatic: Bright Splendor was restored as well, and Virtuous Beauty, Bearing Emblem, and Arrayed Glory were added;

sentences.zh: 以淑媛、淑儀、淑容、昭華、昭儀、昭容、修華、修儀、修容為九嬪；

translations.literal: He made Virtuous Lady of Honor, Virtuous Lady of Elegance, Virtuous Beauty, Bright Splendor, Bright Elegance, Bright Beauty, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, and Cultivated Beauty the Nine Consorts;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Lady of Honor, Virtuous Lady of Elegance, Virtuous Beauty, Bright Splendor, Bright Elegance, Bright Beauty, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, and Cultivated Beauty were constituted as the Nine Consorts;

sentences.zh: 婕妤、容華、充華、承徽、列榮：凡五職，亞九嬪；

translations.literal: Fair Lady, Radiant Splendor, Full Splendor, Bearing Emblem, and Arrayed Glory — five offices in all, next after the Nine Consorts;
translations.idiomatic: Fair Lady, Radiant Splendor, Full Splendor, Bearing Emblem, and Arrayed Glory formed five offices ranking just below the Nine Consorts;

sentences.zh: 美人、才人、良人三職為散役。

translations.literal: Beauty, Talented Lady, and Good Woman — three offices as honorific posts without fixed duties.
translations.idiomatic: Beauty, Talented Lady, and Good Woman were three supernumerary offices.

sentences.zh: 其後，帝留心後房，擬百官，備置內職焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter the emperor devoted attention to the inner quarters, modeling them on the hundred officials and fully establishing inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor turned his attention to the inner palace, patterned its offices on the civil bureaucracy, and filled out the inner establishment.

sentences.zh: 及齊高帝建元元年，有司奏置貴嬪、夫人、貴人為三夫人，修華、修儀、修容、淑妃、淑媛、淑儀、婕妤、容華、充華為九嬪，美人、中才人、才人為散職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi in the first year of Jianyuan, the relevant offices memorialized establishing Noble Consort, Lady, and Noble Lady as the Three Ladies; Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, Cultivated Beauty, Virtuous Consort, Virtuous Lady of Honor, Virtuous Lady of Elegance, Fair Lady, Radiant Splendor, and Full Splendor as the Nine Consorts; Beauty, Central Talented Lady, and Talented Lady as honorific posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan under Emperor Gao of Qi, the relevant offices proposed restoring Noble Consort, Lady, and Noble Lady as the Three Ladies; Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, Cultivated Beauty, Virtuous Consort, Virtuous Lady of Honor, Virtuous Lady of Elegance, Fair Lady, Radiant Splendor, and Full Splendor as the Nine Consorts; and Beauty, Central Talented Lady, and Talented Lady as supernumerary posts.

sentences.zh: 三年，太子宮置三內職：良娣比開國侯，保林比五等侯，才人比駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the third year the crown prince's palace established three inner offices: Good Companion, rank equivalent to Marquis Who Opens a State; Forest Protector, rank equivalent to Fifth-rank Marquis; Talented Lady, rank equivalent to Commandant-Consort of the Stable.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the crown prince's household was given three inner offices: Good Companion, ranked like a marquis who opens a state; Forest Protector, like a fifth-rank marquis; and Talented Lady, like a commandant-consort of the stable.

sentences.zh: 及永明元年，有司奏貴妃、淑妃並加金章紫綬；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming the relevant offices memorialized that Noble Consort and Virtuous Consort were both to receive the golden seal and purple cord;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming the relevant offices proposed that Noble Consort and Virtuous Consort both receive the golden seal and purple cord;

sentences.zh: 佩於寘玉；

translations.literal: worn on the girdle pendant jade;
translations.idiomatic: to be worn with the girdle pendant jade;

sentences.zh: 淑妃舊擬九棘，以淑為溫恭之稱，妃為亞后之名，進同貴妃，以比三司；

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort had formerly been ranked equivalent to the Nine Ministers; since shu means gentle and reverent and fei is a name for one next below the empress, she was promoted to the same level as Noble Consort, equivalent to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort had once been ranked with the Nine Ministers, but because shu denotes gentleness and reverence and fei names one who stands next below the empress, she was raised to Noble Consort's level, equal to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 夫人之號，不殊蕃國；

translations.literal: The title Lady was no different from that used in border kingdoms;
translations.idiomatic: The title Lady was unchanged from that used in tributary states;

sentences.zh: 降淑媛以比九卿。

translations.literal: Virtuous Lady of Honor was lowered, equivalent to the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Lady of Honor was demoted to rank with the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 七年，復置昭容，位在九嬪焉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Bright Beauty was restored, her rank placed among the Nine Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Bright Beauty was restored and given a place among the Nine Consorts.

sentences.zh: 梁武撥亂反正，深鑒奢逸，配德早終，長秋曠位。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang suppressed disorder and restored proper rule, deeply taking warning from extravagance and dissipation; his consort of matching virtue died early, and the office of chief empress stood vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang put down rebellion and restored order, taking hard lesson from luxury and excess; his worthy consort died young, and the empress's seat remained empty.

sentences.zh: 定令制貴妃、貴嬪、貴姬為三夫人；

translations.literal: He established by statute Noble Consort, Noble Lady of Honor, and Noble Concubine as the Three Ladies;
translations.idiomatic: By statute he made Noble Consort, Noble Lady of Honor, and Noble Concubine the Three Ladies;

sentences.zh: 淑媛、淑儀、淑容、昭華、昭儀、昭容、修華、修儀、修容為九嬪；

translations.literal: Virtuous Lady of Honor, Virtuous Lady of Elegance, Virtuous Beauty, Bright Splendor, Bright Elegance, Bright Beauty, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, and Cultivated Beauty as the Nine Consorts;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Lady of Honor, Virtuous Lady of Elegance, Virtuous Beauty, Bright Splendor, Bright Elegance, Bright Beauty, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Elegance, and Cultivated Beauty as the Nine Consorts;

sentences.zh: 婕妤、容華、充華、承徽、列榮為五職；

translations.literal: Fair Lady, Radiant Splendor, Full Splendor, Bearing Emblem, and Arrayed Glory as the Five Offices;
translations.idiomatic: Fair Lady, Radiant Splendor, Full Splendor, Bearing Emblem, and Arrayed Glory as the Five Offices;

sentences.zh: 美人、才人、良人為三職。

translations.literal: Beauty, Talented Lady, and Good Woman as the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Beauty, Talented Lady, and Good Woman as the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 東宮置良娣、保林為二職。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace established Good Companion and Forest Protector as two offices.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's palace had two offices: Good Companion and Forest Protector.

sentences.zh: 及簡文、元帝出自儲蕃，或迫在拘縶，或逼於寇亂；

translations.literal: When Emperors Jianwen and Yuan came from the role of crown prince, some were confined by constraint, others pressed by bandit turmoil;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperors Jianwen and Yuan of Liang rose from the heir apparent, one had been held in confinement and the other driven by invasion and chaos;

sentences.zh: 且妃並先殂，更不建椒閫。

translations.literal: and moreover their consorts had all died first, so they never again established the inner court of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: and because their consorts had already died, neither ever again filled the empress's establishment.

sentences.zh: 陳武光膺天曆，以樸素自居，故後宮員位，其數多闕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen received the Mandate of Heaven; keeping to plain simplicity, the posts of the inner palace were for the most part vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Chen took the throne with a mandate to live plainly, and most inner-palace posts went unfilled.

sentences.zh: 文帝天嘉之後，詔宮職備員。

translations.literal: After the Tianjia era of Emperor Wen, he decreed that palace offices be fully staffed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianjia era, Emperor Wen of Chen ordered the palace offices brought up to full complement.

sentences.zh: 其所制立，無改梁舊。

translations.literal: What was established followed the Liang precedent without change.
translations.idiomatic: The offices he defined followed the Liang model unchanged.

sentences.zh: 編之令文，以為後法。

translations.literal: It was compiled into statutory language to serve as a model for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: These provisions were written into law as a standard for later reigns.

sentences.zh: 然帝性恭儉，而嬪嬙不備，宣帝、後主，無所改作。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's nature was deferential and frugal, and the consorts and ladies were never fully staffed; Emperors Xuan and Houzhu made no alterations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Wen remained modest and austere, and the inner ranks were never fully filled; Emperors Xuan and Houzhu changed nothing.

sentences.zh: 今總綴緝，以立此篇云。

translations.literal: Now I have gathered and arranged these records to establish this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: I have now gathered these records together and set them down in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 南朝宋

translations.literal: Southern Liu Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 孝穆皇后趙安宗

translations.literal: Empress Xiaomu, Zhao Anzong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaomu, Zhao Anzong.

sentences.zh: 宋孝穆趙皇后諱安宗，下邳僮人也。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaomu of Song, née Zhao, personal name Anzong, was a native of Tong in Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaomu of Song, whose personal name was Zhao Anzong, came from Tong in Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 父裔，平原太守。

translations.literal: Her father Yi was Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhao Yi served as administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 后以晉穆帝升平四年嬪于孝皇帝，以產武帝，殂於丹徒官舍，葬晉陵丹徒縣東鄉練壁裏雩山。

translations.literal: The empress entered the inner palace of the Prince of Song in the fourth year of Shengping under Emperor Mu of Jin; because she bore Emperor Wu, she died at the official residence in Dantu and was buried at Yushan in Lianbi Village, Dong District, Dantu county, Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In 360, the fourth year of Shengping under Emperor Mu of Jin, she entered the household of Liu Yu, the future Emperor Wu of Song; she died at the official residence in Dantu after giving birth to him and was buried at Yushan in Lianbi Village, eastern Dantu, Jinling.

sentences.zh: 宋初追崇號諡，陵曰興寧。

translations.literal: In the early Song the title and posthumous name were retroactively bestowed; her tomb was called Xingning.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Song her title and posthumous name were conferred retroactively, and her tomb was named Xingning.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，有司奏追贈裔光祿大夫，加金章紫綬；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu the relevant offices memorialized posthumously enfeoffing Yi as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple cord;
translations.idiomatic: In 421, the second year of Yongchu, the relevant offices proposed posthumously enfeoffing Zhao Yi as grand master for splendid happiness with the golden seal and purple cord;

sentences.zh: 裔命婦孫氏封豫章郡建昌縣君。

translations.literal: Yi's lady, the Lady Sun, was enfeoffed as Lady of Jianchang county, Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's wife, Lady Sun, was enfeoffed as lady of Jianchang county in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 其年，又追封裔臨賀縣侯。

translations.literal: That same year Yi was further enfeoffed as Marquis of Linhe county.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Zhao Yi was further enfeoffed as marquis of Linhe county.

sentences.zh: 裔子倫之自有傳。

translations.literal: Yi's son Lunzhi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Zhao Lunzhi has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 孝懿皇后蕭文壽

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoyi, Xiao Wenshou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoyi, Xiao Wenshou.

sentences.zh: 卓初與趙裔俱贈金紫光祿大夫，又追封封陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Zhuo was at first together with Zhao Yi posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord, and further enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhuo was at first posthumously granted, together with Zhao Yi, the title of grand master for splendid happiness with the golden seal and purple cord, and was later enfeoffed as marquis of Fengyang county.

sentences.zh: 妻下邳趙氏封吳郡壽昌縣君。

translations.literal: His wife, née Zhao of Xiapi, was enfeoffed as Lady of Shouchang county, Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Zhao of Xiapi, was enfeoffed as lady of Shouchang county in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 卓子源之襲爵，源之見子思話傳。

translations.literal: Zhuo's son Yuanzhi inherited the marquisate; Yuanzhi's son Sihua is treated in his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's son Xiao Yuanzhi inherited the marquisate; Yuanzhi's son Xiao Sihua is treated in his own biography.

sentences.zh: 武敬皇后臧愛親

translations.literal: Empress Wujing, Zang Aiqin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wujing, Zang Aiqin.

sentences.zh: 武敬臧皇后諱愛親，東莞人也。

translations.literal: Empress Wujing of the Zang clan, personal name Aiqin, was a native of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wujing of the Zang clan, whose personal name was Aiqin, came from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 祖汪，尚書郎，父雋，郡功曹。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Wang was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; her father Juan was Merit Officer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Zang Wang was a gentleman of the masters of writing; her father Zang Juan served as merit officer of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 后適武帝，生會稽宣長公主興弟。

translations.literal: The empress was given in marriage to Emperor Wu and bore Princess Xingdi of Kuaiji, titled Xuanchang.
translations.idiomatic: She married Liu Yu, the future Emperor Wu of Song, and bore Princess Xingdi of Kuaiji, titled Xuanchang.

sentences.zh: 帝以儉正率下，后恭謹不違。

translations.literal: The emperor was frugal and upright in leading those below; the empress was reverent and careful, never transgressing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led by frugal example; the empress was reverent and careful and never overstepped her place.

sentences.zh: 義熙四年正月甲子，殂於東城，追贈豫章公夫人，還葬丹徒。

translations.literal: On day jiazi of the first month of the fourth year of Yixi she died in the Eastern City; she was posthumously granted the title Lady of the Duke of Yuzhang and returned for burial to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the first month in 408, the fourth year of Yixi, she died in the Eastern City; she was posthumously made lady of the Duke of Yuzhang and returned for burial to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 帝臨崩，遺詔留葬建鄴。

translations.literal: When the emperor was on the verge of death, his testamentary edict ordered that she be retained for burial at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the emperor left orders that she be kept for burial at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 於是備法駕迎梓宮，祔葬初寧陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon the full imperial escort was prepared to receive the coffin, and she was buried alongside at Chuning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The full imperial escort was then sent to receive her coffin, and she was buried beside him at Chuning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 宋初追贈雋金紫光祿大夫，妻高密叔孫氏遷陵永平鄉君。

translations.literal: In the early Song Juan was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord; his wife, née Shusun of Gaomi, was promoted to Lady Yongping Township.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Song, Juan was posthumously enfeoffed as grand master for splendid happiness with the golden seal and purple cord, and his wife, née Shusun of Gaomi, was raised to lady of Yongping township.

sentences.zh: 雋子燾、熹，並自有傳。

translations.literal: Juan's sons Tao and Xi each have their own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's sons Zang Tao and Zang Xi each have their own biography.

sentences.zh: 武帝夫人張闕

translations.literal: Lady Zhang of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 武帝張夫人，諱闕，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang of Emperor Wu, personal name Que, was from an unknown place.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang of Emperor Wu, whose personal name was Que, was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 生少帝及義興恭長公主惠媛。

translations.literal: She bore the Lesser Emperor and Princess Huiyuan of Yixing, titled Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Liu Yifu, the lesser emperor, and Princess Huiyuan of Yixing, titled Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 永初元年拜夫人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu she was appointed Lady.
translations.idiomatic: In 420, the first year of Yongchu, she was appointed Lady.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，有司奏上尊號為皇太后，宮曰永樂。

translations.literal: When the Lesser Emperor took the throne, the relevant offices memorialized bestowing on her the honorific title Empress Dowager; her palace was Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: When the lesser emperor succeeded, the relevant offices proposed honoring her as empress dowager and assigning her Yongle Palace.

sentences.zh: 少帝廢，太后還璽紱，隨居吳郡。

translations.literal: When the Lesser Emperor was deposed, the empress dowager returned the seals and regalia and went to live in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the lesser emperor was deposed, she surrendered the seals and regalia and withdrew to Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉元年，拜營陽國太妃，二年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen she was appointed Grand Princess Consort of Yingyang; in the second year she died.
translations.idiomatic: In 424, the first year of Yuanjia, Emperor Wen made her grand princess consort of Yingyang; she died the following year.

sentences.zh: 文章皇太后胡道安

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenzhang, Hu Dao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenzhang, Hu Dao'an.

sentences.zh: 文章胡太后諱道安，淮南人也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenzhang of the Hu clan, personal name Dao'an, was a native of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenzhang of the Hu clan, whose personal name was Dao'an, came from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，武帝所納。

translations.literal: In the early Yixi era she was taken in by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yixi era she entered the household of Liu Yu, the future Emperor Wu of Song.

sentences.zh: 文帝生五年，被譴賜死，葬丹徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen had lived five years, she was rebuked and ordered to die; she was buried at Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: When her son, the future Emperor Wen, was five years old, she was condemned and ordered to take her own life; she was buried at Dantu.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，追贈婕妤。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, she was posthumously granted Fair Lady.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne, she was posthumously made Fair Lady.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，有司奏上尊號曰：「章皇太后」，陵曰：「熙寧」，立廟建鄴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, the relevant offices memorialized the honorific title: "Empress Dowager Wenzhang"; her tomb was called Xining, and a temple was established at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, the relevant offices proposed honoring her as Empress Dowager Wenzhang, naming her tomb Xining and building a temple for her at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 少帝皇后司馬茂英

translations.literal: Empress of the Lesser Emperor, Sima Maoying.
translations.idiomatic: Empress of the lesser emperor, Sima Maoying.

sentences.zh: 文元皇后袁齊媯

translations.literal: Empress Wenyuan, Yuan Qiji.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenyuan, Yuan Qiji.

sentences.zh: 文元袁皇后諱齊媯，陳郡陽夏人，左光祿大夫湛之庶女也。

translations.literal: Empress Wenyuan of the Yuan clan, personal name Qiji, was from Yangxia in Chen commandery, a secondary daughter of Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenyuan of the Yuan clan, whose personal name was Qiji, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery and was a secondary daughter of Yuan Zhanzhi, left grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 母本卑賤，后年至六歲方見舉。

translations.literal: Her mother's origin was lowly; the empress was not acknowledged until she was six.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother came from humble stock, and the empress was not formally recognized in the household until she was six.

sentences.zh: 後適文帝，初拜宜都王妃，生子劭、東陽獻公主英娥。

translations.literal: Later she was given in marriage to Emperor Wen; at first she was appointed Princess of Yidu, and bore Shao and Princess Ying'e of Dongyang, titled Xian.
translations.idiomatic: She later married Emperor Wen and was first made princess of Yidu; she bore Liu Shao and Princess Ying'e of Dongyang, titled Xian.

sentences.zh: 上待后恩禮甚篤，袁氏貧薄，后每就上求錢帛以贍之。

translations.literal: The emperor treated the empress with deep favor and ceremony; the Yuan clan were poor and of few means, and whenever the empress went to the emperor she would request money and silks to support them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved and honored her deeply; the Yuan family were poor, and whenever she visited him she asked for money and silk to support them.

sentences.zh: 上性儉，所得不過五三萬、五三十匹。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was frugal; what she received never exceeded fifty or thirty thousand cash and fifty or thirty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, he never gave her more than thirty to fifty thousand cash or thirty to fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 後潘淑妃有寵，愛傾後宮，咸言所求無不得。

translations.literal: Later when Virtuous Consort Pan gained favor, love filled the rear palace, and all said her requests were never refused.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Virtuous Consort Pan won the emperor's favor, the whole inner palace said that whatever she asked for was granted.

sentences.zh: 后聞之，未知信否，乃因潘求三十萬錢與家，以觀上意，宿昔便得。

translations.literal: When the empress heard this, not knowing whether to believe it, she thereupon asked Pan for three hundred thousand cash for her family to test the emperor's intent — and within a single night she received it.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this and unsure whether to believe it, the empress asked Pan to request three hundred thousand cash for her family as a test of the emperor's mind — and the money arrived overnight.

sentences.zh: 因此恚恨稱疾，不復見上，遂憤恚成疾。

translations.literal: Because of this she nursed resentment, claimed illness, and no longer saw the emperor, until anger and resentment brought on real sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Stung by this, she claimed illness and refused to see the emperor again, until resentment and rage made her genuinely ill.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十七年疾篤，上執手流涕，問所欲言。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia her illness grew grave; the emperor took her hand with tears and asked what she wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia she fell critically ill; the emperor clasped her hand in tears and asked what she wanted to say.

sentences.zh: 后視上良久，乃引被覆面，崩于顯陽殿。

translations.literal: The empress gazed at the emperor for a long while, then drew the coverlet over her face and died in Xianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The empress looked at him a long while, then pulled the coverlet over her face and died in Xianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 上甚悼痛之，詔前永嘉太守顏延之為哀策，文甚麗。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned her deeply and ordered Yan Yanzhi, former administrator of Yongjia, to compose a funeral elegy; the text was very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply grieved, the emperor ordered Yan Yanzhi, former administrator of Yongjia, to write a funeral elegy of exceptional beauty.

sentences.zh: 及奏，上自益「撫存悼亡，感今懷昔。

translations.literal: When it was submitted, the emperor himself added, "Comfort the living and mourn the dead; moved by the present, I think of the past."
translations.idiomatic: When the elegy was presented, the emperor added eight characters of his own: "Comfort the living and mourn the dead; moved by the present, I think of the past."

sentences.zh: 」八字以致意焉。

translations.literal: These eight characters served to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: With these eight characters he made his meaning plain.

sentences.zh: 有司奏諡宣皇后，詔諡曰元。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized the posthumous title Empress Xuan; an edict granted the temple name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices proposed the posthumous title Empress Xuan, and an edict fixed her temple name as Yuan.

sentences.zh: 初，后生劭，自詳視之，使馳白帝：「此兒形貌異常，必破國亡家，不可舉。

translations.literal: At first, when the empress bore Shao, she examined him closely herself and sent a messenger in haste to tell the emperor: "This child's form and appearance are unusual; he will surely ruin the state and destroy the family — he must not be raised."
translations.idiomatic: When she first gave birth to Shao, she studied him closely and sent a messenger racing to the emperor: "This child's looks are strange; he will ruin the realm and end the house — he must not be kept."

sentences.zh: 」便欲殺之。

translations.literal: She then wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: She then wanted to kill the child.

sentences.zh: 文帝狼狽至後殿戶外，手掇幔禁之乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen rushed in disarray to the outer door of the rear hall, seized the curtain with his hand, and forbade it — only then did she stop.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen came in haste to the rear hall's outer door, caught the curtain in his hand, and forbade her — only then did she desist.

sentences.zh: 后亡後，常有小小靈應。

translations.literal: After the empress's death there were often small spiritual manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: After her death there were frequent minor signs of her spirit.

sentences.zh: 明帝所生沈美人嘗以非罪見責，應賜死，從後昔所住徽音殿前度。

translations.literal: The Beauty Shen, who had borne Emperor Ming, was once punished for a fault that was no crime and was to be granted death; she passed before the Huiyin Hall where the empress had once lived.
translations.idiomatic: Shen the Beauty, Emperor Ming's mother, was once condemned for a faultless offense and ordered to die; she was led past Huiyin Hall, where the late empress had once dwelt.

sentences.zh: 此殿有五間，自后崩後常閉。

translations.literal: This hall had five bays; since the empress's death it had always been kept closed.
translations.idiomatic: The hall had five bays and had remained shut since the empress died.

sentences.zh: 美人至殿前流涕大言曰：「今日無罪就死，先後若有靈當知之。

translations.literal: When the Beauty reached the hall she wept and cried out loudly: "Today I am put to death without guilt; if the late empress has a spirit, let her know of this."
translations.idiomatic: At the hall she wept and cried aloud: "Today I die though I am guiltless; if the late empress's spirit lives, let it know."

sentences.zh: 」殿戶應聲豁然開，職掌者遽白文帝，驚往視之，美人乃得釋。

translations.literal: The hall doors at once flew open in response; the attendants hurried to report to Emperor Wen, who came in alarm to look — and the Beauty was released.
translations.idiomatic: The hall doors burst open at once; attendants rushed to tell Emperor Wen, who came in alarm to see — and the Beauty was spared.

sentences.zh: 大明五年，孝武乃詔追后之所生外祖親王夫人為豫章郡新淦平樂鄉君，又詔趙、蕭、臧光祿、袁敬公、平樂鄉君墓，先未給塋戶，各給蠻戶三以供灑掃。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu ordered that the empress's maternal grandmother Lady Wang be posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Pingle township in Xingan county, Yuzhang commandery; he also ordered that for the tombs of Zhao, Xiao, Zang the Guanglu rank-holder, Duke Jing of Yuan, and the Lady of Pingle township — which had not previously been assigned grave households — each should be given three barbarian households for sprinkling and sweeping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu posthumously enfeoffed the empress's maternal grandmother Lady Wang as lady of Pingle township in Xingan, Yuzhang commandery, and ordered that the tombs of Zhao, Xiao, Zang the grand master for splendid happiness, Duke Jing of Yuan, and the lady of Pingle township — none yet assigned grave households — each receive three barbarian households for upkeep.

sentences.zh: 後公湛之自有傳。

translations.literal: His Excellency Zhanzhi has a separate biography later.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhanzhi is treated in a separate biography later in the work.

sentences.zh: 潘淑妃

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Pan.

sentences.zh: 潘淑妃者，本以貌進，始未見賞。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Pan had entered the palace on her beauty; at first she received no favor.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Pan had been taken into the palace for her looks, but at first won no favor.

sentences.zh: 帝好乘羊車經諸房，淑妃每莊飾褰帷以候，並密令左右以鹹水灑地。

translations.literal: The emperor liked to ride in a goat-cart through the women's quarters; the Virtuous Consort each time dressed carefully, lifted the curtain, and waited, and secretly ordered her attendants to sprinkle the ground with salt water.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor liked to ride a goat-cart through the inner quarters; each time she dressed with care, lifted the curtain, and waited, while secretly ordering attendants to sprinkle the ground with salt water.

sentences.zh: 帝每至戶，羊輒舐地不去。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor reached her door, the goats would lick the ground and refuse to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor reached her door, the goats would lick the salted ground and linger.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「羊乃為汝徘徊，況於人乎。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Even the goats linger for your sake — how much more so a man!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Even the goats pause for you — how much more should a man!"

sentences.zh: 」于此愛傾後宮。

translations.literal: From that point his love for her surpassed all others in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his favor for her eclipsed every other woman in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 孝武昭皇太后路惠男

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhaowu Lu Hui'nan of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhaowu Lu Hui'nan of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 孝武昭路太后諱惠男，丹陽建康人也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhaowu of the Lu clan, personal name Hui'nan, was a native of Jiankang in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhaowu of the Lu clan, whose personal name was Hui'nan, came from Jiankang in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 以色貌選入後宮，生孝武帝，拜為淑媛。

translations.literal: Chosen for the rear palace on account of her looks, she bore Emperor Xiaowu and was appointed Virtuous Lady of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: Taken into the inner palace for her beauty, she bore the future Emperor Xiaowu and was made virtuous lady of honor.

sentences.zh: 及年長，無寵，常隨孝武出蕃。

translations.literal: When he grew older and she had no favor, she often followed Xiaowu when he went out to his princely fief.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up she fell from favor and often accompanied him when he was sent to govern a princely domain.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，有司奏奉尊號曰太后，宮曰崇憲。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu took the throne, the relevant offices memorialized that she be honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Chongxian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu succeeded, the relevant offices proposed honoring her as empress dowager and assigning her Chongxian Palace.

sentences.zh: 太后居顯陽殿，上於閨房之內禮敬甚寡，有所禦幸，或留止太后房內，故人間咸有醜聲。

translations.literal: The empress dowager lived in Xianyang Hall; within the inner quarters the emperor showed her very little ceremonial respect, and when he visited her he sometimes stayed overnight in her chamber — so among the people there were ugly rumors.
translations.idiomatic: She dwelt in Xianyang Hall; within the private quarters the emperor paid her scant formal respect, and when he visited her he sometimes spent the night in her rooms — so ugly rumors spread among the people.

sentences.zh: 宮掖事秘，亦莫能辨也。

translations.literal: Palace affairs were secret, and no one could verify the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-palace matters were closely guarded, and no one could settle what was true.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，追贈太后父興之散騎常侍，興之妻余杭縣廣昌鄉君。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, the empress dowager's father Xingzhi was posthumously granted attendant at the palace gate, and Xingzhi's wife was made Lady of Guangchang township in Yuhang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian her father Xingzhi was posthumously made attendant at the palace gate, and his wife was enfeoffed as lady of Guangchang township in Yuhang county.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，太后弟子撫軍參軍瓊之上表自陳。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming, the empress dowager's younger brother's son Qiong, a staff member of the army of suppression, submitted a memorial in his own name.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming her nephew Qiong, a staff officer on the army of suppression, memorialized in his own name.

sentences.zh: 有司承旨，奏贈瓊之父道慶給事中，瓊之及弟休之、茂之並居顯職。

translations.literal: The relevant offices, following the imperial intent, memorialized posthumously granting Qiong's father Daoqing attendant within the palace, and Qiong together with his brothers Xiuzhi and Maozhi all received prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on the emperor's wish, the relevant offices posthumously made Qiong's father Daoqing attendant within the palace and placed Qiong and his brothers Xiuzhi and Maozhi in high office.

sentences.zh: 太后頗豫政事，賜與瓊之等財物，家累千金，居處器服與帝子相侔。

translations.literal: The empress dowager took part in government affairs and bestowed wealth on Qiong and the others; their household accumulated thousands in gold, and their dwellings, vessels, and robes matched those of the emperor's sons.
translations.idiomatic: She meddled in government and lavished goods on Qiong and his kin until their household held thousands in gold and their homes, furnishings, and dress rivaled the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 大明五年，太后隨上巡南豫州，妃主以下並從。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming the empress dowager accompanied the emperor on a tour of southern Yuzhou; princesses and ladies of rank and below all followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming she accompanied the emperor on a tour of southern Yuzhou, with princesses and ladies of rank and below in attendance.

sentences.zh: 廢帝立，號太皇太后。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor took the throne, she was styled grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor succeeded, she was honored as grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 明帝踐阼，號崇憲太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, she was styled Empress Dowager Chongxian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, she was styled Empress Dowager Chongxian.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉安王子勳未平，巫者謂宜開昭太后陵，毀去梓宮以厭勝。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Prince Jin'an Zixun had not yet been pacified, a shaman said that the tomb of Empress Dowager Zhaowu should be opened and the inner coffin removed as a counter-spell.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Prince Jin'an Zixun's rebellion was still unsettled, a shaman said the tomb of Empress Dowager Zhaowu should be opened and the inner coffin removed to break the spell.

sentences.zh: 修復倉卒，不得如禮。

translations.literal: The repairs were hurried and could not follow proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The work was done in haste and could not observe full rites.

sentences.zh: 上性忌，慮將來致災，泰始四年夏，詔有司曰：「崇憲昭太后修甯陵地，大明之世，久所考卜。

translations.literal: The emperor was superstitious by nature and feared future calamity; in summer of the fourth year of Taishi he issued an edict to the relevant offices: "The tomb site of Empress Dowager Chongxian Zhaowu at Xiuning Mausoleum was long ago divined and chosen during the Daming era."
translations.idiomatic: Superstitious by nature and fearing later disaster, in the summer of the fourth year of Taishi he ordered the relevant offices: "The burial ground of Empress Dowager Chongxian Zhaowu at Xiuning Mausoleum was divined and chosen long ago in the Daming era."

sentences.zh: 前歲遭諸蕃之難，禮從權宜，未暇營改，而塋隧之所，山原卑陋，可式遵舊典，以禮改創。

translations.literal: Last year, because of the troubles of the various princes, ritual was adjusted as expedience required and there was no time to rebuild; yet the burial place lies on low, poor ground — we may properly follow the old statutes and rebuild it according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's troubles among the princes forced ritual aside, and there was no time to rebuild; yet the site is low and poor — let the old statutes be followed and the tomb remade in proper form.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏請「修甯陵玄宮補葺毀壞，權施油殿，暫出梓宮，事畢即窆」。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized requesting "repair of the deep chamber at Xiuning Mausoleum and mending of damage, temporarily erecting an oiled hall and temporarily removing the inner coffin; when the work is finished, reinter at once."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices proposed repairing the deep chamber at Xiuning Mausoleum, patching what was damaged, temporarily erecting an oiled hall and removing the inner coffin, and reinterring it as soon as the work was done.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was approved.

sentences.zh: 廢帝景和中，又追贈興之侍中、金紫光祿大夫，諡曰孝侯。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era under the deposed emperor, Xingzhi was posthumously granted palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness with the golden seal and purple cord, with the posthumous title Marquis Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe era under the deposed emperor, Xingzhi was posthumously made palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness with the golden seal and purple cord, with the posthumous title Marquis Xiao.

sentences.zh: 道慶光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，諡曰敬侯。

translations.literal: Daoqing was granted grand master for splendid happiness and grand marshal with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing was posthumously made grand master for splendid happiness and grand marshal with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 道慶女為皇后，以休之為侍中。

translations.literal: Daoqing's daughter became empress, and Xiuzhi was made palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing's daughter was made empress, and Xiuzhi was appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 明宣皇太后沈容姬

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Mingxuan Shen Rongji.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Mingxuan Shen Rongji.

sentences.zh: 明宣沈太后諱容姬，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Mingxuan of the Shen clan, personal name Rongji, was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Mingxuan of the Shen clan, whose personal name was Rongji, was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 為文帝美人，生明帝，拜婕妤。

translations.literal: She was a Beauty of Emperor Wen, bore Emperor Ming, and was appointed Fair Lady.
translations.idiomatic: A beauty of Emperor Wen, she bore the future Emperor Ming and was made fair lady.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三十年卒，葬建康之莫府山。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia she died and was buried on Mount Mofu at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the thirtieth year of Yuanjia and was buried on Mount Mofu near Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，追贈湘東國太妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, she was posthumously granted Grand Consort of the Xiangdong kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu succeeded, she was posthumously made grand consort of the Xiangdong kingdom.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，有司奏上尊號為皇太后，諡曰宣，陵號崇寧。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, the relevant offices memorialized that she be honored as empress dowager; her posthumous title was Xuan and her tomb was called Chongning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, the relevant offices proposed honoring her as empress dowager with the posthumous title Xuan and the tomb name Chongning.

sentences.zh: 孝武文穆皇后王憲嫄

translations.literal: Empress Wenmu Wang Xianyuan of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenmu Wang Xianyuan of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，后率六宮躬桑於西郊，皇太后觀禮，妃主以下並加班錫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming the empress led the Six Palaces in personally picking mulberry leaves at the western suburb; the empress dowager observed the rites, and princesses and ladies of rank and below all received additional gifts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming the empress led the inner palace in picking mulberry leaves at the western suburb while the empress dowager watched the rites; princesses and ladies of rank and below all received extra gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，尊曰皇太后，宮曰永訓。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Yongxun.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor succeeded, she was honored as empress dowager and assigned Yongxun Palace.

sentences.zh: 其年崩于含章殿，祔葬景寧陵。

translations.literal: That same year she died in Hanzhang Hall and was buried beside the emperor at Jingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: That same year she died in Hanzhang Hall and was buried with the emperor at Jingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 父偃別有傳。

translations.literal: Her father Yan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wang Yan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 殷淑儀

translations.literal: Virtuous Lady Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Lady Yin.

sentences.zh: 時有巫者能見鬼，說帝言貴妃可致。

translations.literal: At the time there was a shaman who could see ghosts; he told the emperor that the imperial consort could be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman who claimed to see ghosts told the emperor the late consort could be brought back.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，令召之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered her summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed and ordered the rite performed.

sentences.zh: 有少頃，果於帷中見形如平生。

translations.literal: After a little while, within the curtain a form indeed appeared as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a figure appeared within the curtain, looking as she had in life.

sentences.zh: 帝欲與之言，默然不對。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to speak with her, but she remained silent and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried to speak with her, but she stayed silent and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 將執手，奄然便歇，帝尤哽恨，於是擬李夫人賦以寄意焉。

translations.literal: As he was about to take her hand, she suddenly vanished; the emperor grieved all the more, and thereupon modeled his feelings on the Rhapsody on Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: As he reached for her hand she vanished; stricken with regret, he wrote a piece modeled on the Rhapsody on Lady Li to pour out his grief.

sentences.zh: 謝莊作哀策文奏之，帝臥覽讀，起坐流涕曰：「不謂當今復有此才。

translations.literal: Xie Zhuang composed a funeral elegy and submitted it; the emperor read it while lying down, then sat up with tears and said, "I did not expect that in our day there should still be such talent."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhuang wrote a funeral elegy and presented it; the emperor read it in bed, then sat up in tears and said, "I did not think such talent still existed in our time."

sentences.zh: 」都下傳寫，紙墨為之貴。

translations.literal: Copies spread through the capital, and paper and ink rose in price on their account.
translations.idiomatic: Copies raced through the capital, and paper and ink soared in price.

sentences.zh: 或云，貴妃是殷琰家人入義宣家，義宣敗入宮云。

translations.literal: Some say the consort was a member of Yin Yan's household who entered the house of Prince Yixuan, and after Yixuan's defeat entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Some say she was kin of Yin Yan who entered Prince Yixuan's household and, after his fall, was taken into the palace.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝皇后何令婉

translations.literal: Empress He Lingwan of the Former Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He Lingwan of the former deposed emperor.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝何皇后諱令婉，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: Empress He of the former deposed emperor, personal name Lingwan, was a native of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He of the former deposed emperor, whose personal name was Lingwan, came from Qian in Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，納為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian she was taken in as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian she was made crown princess.

sentences.zh: 大明五年，薨於東宮徽光殿，諡曰獻妃。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming she died in Huiguang Hall in the Eastern Palace and was granted the posthumous title Consort Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming she died in Huiguang Hall in the Eastern Palace and received the posthumous title Consort Xian.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，追崇曰獻皇后。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor took the throne, she was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor succeeded, she was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 明帝踐阼，遷后與廢帝合葬龍山北。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, the empress was moved and buried together with the deposed emperor north of Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, she was reinterred beside the deposed emperor north of Longshan.

sentences.zh: 瑀兄子衍性躁動，位黃門郎，拜竟，求司徒司馬；

translations.literal: Yu Yu's brother's son Yan was restless by nature; when appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, as soon as the commission was issued he requested to be secretary of the minister of works;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu's nephew Yan was impulsive by nature; once made gentleman at the yellow gates, he immediately asked to be secretary of the minister of works;

sentences.zh: 得司馬，復求太子右率；

translations.literal: Having obtained that post, he requested in turn to be right leader of the crown prince's guard;
translations.idiomatic: given that office, he next demanded the post of right leader of the crown prince's guard;

sentences.zh: 拜一二日，復求侍中。

translations.literal: Within a day or two of receiving the appointment, he requested the post of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: a day or two after that appointment he asked to be palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，求進無已。

translations.literal: Within ten days he sought promotion without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he pressed for advancement without pause.

sentences.zh: 不得侍中，以怨詈賜死。

translations.literal: Denied the post of palace attendant, he cursed in resentment and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Denied the post of palace attendant, he cursed in anger and was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 明恭皇后王貞風

translations.literal: Empress Minggong Wang Zhenfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Minggong Wang Zhenfeng.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝太妃陳妙登

translations.literal: Grand Consort Chen Miaodeng of the Later Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Chen Miaodeng of the later deposed emperor.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝皇后江簡珪

translations.literal: Empress Jiang Jiangui of the Later Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jiang Jiangui of the later deposed emperor.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝江皇后諱簡珪，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Empress Jiang of the later deposed emperor, personal name Jiangui, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jiang of the later deposed emperor, whose personal name was Jiangui, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，明帝訪太子妃而雅信小數，名家女多不合。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi, Emperor Ming sought a crown princess but trusted divination by numbers; daughters of eminent families mostly did not match auspiciously.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi Emperor Ming sought a crown princess but relied on numerology; daughters of great houses mostly failed the auguries.

sentences.zh: 江氏雖為華族，而后父祖並已亡，弟又弱小，以卜筮吉，故為太子納之。

translations.literal: Though the Jiang clan were a splendid family, the empress's father and grandfather were both already dead and her younger brother was still young; because divination proved auspicious, she was taken as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Jiang were a noble clan, her father and grandfather were dead and her younger brother still a child; because the divination was favorable, she was chosen as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜皇太子妃，諷朝士州郡皆令獻物，多者將直百金。

translations.literal: In the sixth year she was made crown princess; officials in the capital and in the provinces were all hinted to present gifts, with the most generous worth nearly a hundred gold pieces.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year she became crown princess; courtiers and provincial officials were quietly told to send gifts, the richest worth nearly a hundred gold pieces.

sentences.zh: 始興太守孫奉伯止獻琴書，其外無餘物。

translations.literal: Sun Fengbo, administrator of Shixing, presented only a zither and books — nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fengbo, administrator of Shixing, sent only a zither and books and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，封藥賜死，既而原之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, sealed poison and ordered him to die, but afterward pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, sealed poison and ordered his death, then afterward relented.

sentences.zh: 太子即帝位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the crown prince took the throne, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince became emperor, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 帝既廢，降后為蒼梧王妃。

translations.literal: After the emperor was deposed, the empress was demoted to princess consort of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's deposition she was reduced to princess consort of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 祖智深自有傳。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Zhishen has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Jiang Zhishen has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 順太妃陳法容

translations.literal: Grand Consort Chen Farong of Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Chen Farong of Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 順皇后謝梵境

translations.literal: Empress Xie Fanjing of Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xie Fanjing of Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 順謝皇后諱梵境，陳郡陽夏人。

translations.literal: Empress Xie of Emperor Shun, personal name Fanjing, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xie of Emperor Shun, whose personal name was Fanjing, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 右光祿大夫莊之孫也。

translations.literal: She was the granddaughter of Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: She was a granddaughter of Xie Zhuang, right grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 父揚，車騎功曹。

translations.literal: Her father Yang was a merit officer on the staff of the commander of chariots and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yang was a merit officer on the staff of the commander of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 升明二年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 順帝禪位，降為汝陰王妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun abdicated, she was demoted to princess consort of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun abdicated the throne, she was reduced to princess consort of Runan.

sentences.zh: 祖莊自有傳。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Zhuang has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Xie Zhuang has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 南朝齊

translations.literal: Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 宣孝皇后陳道止

translations.literal: Empress Xuanxiao Chen Daozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanxiao Chen Daozhi.

sentences.zh: 齊宣孝陳皇后諱道止，臨淮東陽人，魏司徒矯之後也。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanxiao of the Chen clan, personal name Daozhi, was a native of Dongyang in Linhuai and a descendant of Jiao, minister of works of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanxiao of the Chen clan, whose personal name was Daozhi, came from Dongyang in Linhuai commandery and was descended from Chen Jiao, minister of works of Wei.

sentences.zh: 后家貧，少勤織作，家人矜其勞，或止之，后終不改。

translations.literal: The empress's family was poor; from youth she diligently wove and worked. Her kin took pity on her labor and sometimes tried to stop her, but the empress never changed.
translations.idiomatic: Her family was poor, and from girlhood she wove and worked without rest. Relatives pitied her toil and tried to make her stop, but she never changed her ways.

sentences.zh: 嫁于宣帝。

translations.literal: She was married to Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: She married Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 宣帝庶生子衡陽元王道度、始安貞王道生，后生高帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan had borne by concubines Prince Daodu of Hengyang and Prince Daosheng of Shi'an; afterward she bore Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan's sons by concubines were Prince Daodu of Hengyang and Prince Daosheng of Shi'an; afterward she bore Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 高帝年二歲，乳人乏乳，后夢人以兩甌麻粥與之，覺而乳驚，因此豐足。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao was two years old, his wet nurse had insufficient milk. The empress dreamed that someone gave her two bowls of hemp porridge; when she awoke her milk was abundant, and from this it became plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao was two, his wet nurse could not supply enough milk. The empress dreamed that someone handed her two bowls of hemp porridge; she awoke to find her milk flowing freely, and from then on it was ample.

sentences.zh: 宣帝從任在外，后常留家，有相者謂后曰：「夫人有貴子而不見之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan was away on assignment; the empress often remained at home. A physiognomist told the empress: "My lady has an eminent son, but I have not seen him."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was posted away from home while the empress stayed behind. A physiognomist told her, "My lady has a son of great rank, yet I have not laid eyes on him."

sentences.zh: 」后歎曰：「我三子，誰當應之？

translations.literal: The empress sighed and said: "I have three sons — which of them should it be?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress sighed. "I have three sons — which of them can it be?"

sentences.zh: 」呼高帝小字曰：「政應是汝耳。」

translations.literal: She called Emperor Gao by his childhood name and said: "It must be you after all."
translations.idiomatic: She called Emperor Gao by his childhood name and said, "It must be you."

sentences.zh: 永明九年，詔太廟四時祭，宣皇帝薦起面餅鴨榷，孝皇后薦筍鴨卵脯醬炙白肉，高皇帝薦肉膾葅羹，昭皇后薦茗粣炙魚。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming an edict ordered seasonal sacrifices at the imperial temple: Emperor Xuan was to offer risen dough cakes, duck, and pickled fruits; Empress Xiao was to offer bamboo shoots, duck eggs, dried meat, sauce, and roasted white meat; Emperor Gao was to offer minced meat, pickled vegetables, and broth; Empress Liu was to offer tea, rice cakes, and roasted fish.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongming an edict fixed the offerings for the four seasonal sacrifices at the imperial temple: Emperor Xuan — risen dough cakes, duck, and pickled fruits; Empress Xiao — bamboo shoots, duck eggs, dried meat, sauce, and roasted white meat; Emperor Gao — minced meat, pickled vegetables, and broth; Empress Liu — tea, rice cakes, and roasted fish.

sentences.zh: 並生平所嗜也。

translations.literal: Each was what they had loved in life.
translations.idiomatic: Each offering was a food they had loved in life.

sentences.zh: 高昭皇后劉智容

translations.literal: Empress Gaozhao Liu Zhirong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gaozhao Liu Zhirong.

sentences.zh: 高昭劉皇后諱智容，廣陵人也。

translations.literal: Empress Gaozhao of the Liu clan, personal name Zhirong, was a native of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gaozhao of the Liu clan, whose personal name was Zhirong, came from Guangling.

sentences.zh: 祖玄之，父壽之，並員外郎。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Xuanzhi and her father Shouzhi were both supernumerary gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Liu Xuanzhi and her father Liu Shouzhi were both supernumerary gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 后母桓氏，夢吞玉勝生后，時有紫光滿室，以告壽之。

translations.literal: The empress's mother, of the Huan clan, dreamed that she swallowed a jade hair ornament and then gave birth to the empress; at the time purple light filled the room, and she told Shouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother, Lady Huan, dreamed that she swallowed a jade ornament and then bore the empress; purple light filled the room, and she told Shouzhi.

sentences.zh: 壽之曰：「恨非是男。

translations.literal: Shouzhi said: "I regret that it is not a boy."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhi said, "Pity it is not a son."

sentences.zh: 」桓笑曰：「雖女亦足興家矣。

translations.literal: Huan smiled and said: "Though a girl, she is enough to raise up the family."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huan smiled and said, "Even a daughter can lift a house."

sentences.zh: 」後寢臥，見有羽蓋蔭其上，家人試察之，常見其上掩藹如有雲氣。

translations.literal: Later while she slept they saw a feathered canopy shading her; when the family tried to observe, they often saw a misty canopy like cloud vapor above her.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as she slept, a feathered canopy seemed to shade her; when the household looked closely, a cloudy mist often hung above her bed.

sentences.zh: 武穆皇后裴惠昭

translations.literal: Empress Wumu Pei Huizhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wumu Pei Huizhao.

sentences.zh: 武穆裴皇后諱惠昭，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Empress Wumu of the Pei clan, personal name Huizhao, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wumu of the Pei clan, whose personal name was Huizhao, came from Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖封之，給事中。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Fengzhi was an attendant within the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Pei Fengzhi was an attendant within the gates.

sentences.zh: 父璣之，左軍參軍。

translations.literal: Her father Jizhi was a staff officer of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Pei Jizhi was a staff officer of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 后少與豫章王妃庾氏為娣姒，庾氏勤女工，奉事高昭後恭謹不倦，后不能及，故不為舅姑所重，武帝亦薄焉。

translations.literal: In youth the empress and Lady Yu, consort of the Prince of Yuzhang, were sisters-in-law. Lady Yu was diligent at women's crafts and served Empress Gaozhao with tireless reverence; the empress could not match her, so she was not valued by her parents-in-law, and Emperor Wu also looked down on her.
translations.idiomatic: In youth she and Lady Yu, consort of the Prince of Yuzhang, were sisters-in-law. Lady Yu was skilled at women's work and served Empress Gaozhao with tireless devotion; the empress could not equal her, so her in-laws held her lightly and Emperor Wu thought little of her.

sentences.zh: 舊顯陽、昭陽二殿，太后皇后所居也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Xianyang and Zhaoyang halls were where the empress dowager and empress dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Xianyang and Zhaoyang halls were the quarters of the empress dowager and empress.

sentences.zh: 永明中無太后皇后，羊貴嬪居昭陽殿西，范貴妃居昭陽殿東，寵姬荀昭華居鳳華柏殿。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era there was no empress dowager or empress; Noble Consort Yang lived in the west wing of Zhaoyang Hall, Noble Consort Fan in the east wing of Zhaoyang Hall, and the favored concubine Xun Zhaohua in Fenghua Bai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming there was neither empress dowager nor empress; Noble Consort Yang occupied the west wing of Zhaoyang Hall, Noble Consort Fan the east wing, and the favored concubine Xun Zhaohua Fenghua Bai Hall.

sentences.zh: 宮內禦所居壽昌畫殿南閣，置白鷺鼓吹二部，幹光殿東西頭，置鍾磬兩廂，皆宴樂處也。

translations.literal: Within the palace, in the south pavilion of the Painted Hall of Shouchang where the emperor dwelt, two companies of egret-drummers and wind players were stationed; at the east and west ends of Ganshan Hall, bell and chime chambers were set up — all were places for feasting and music.
translations.idiomatic: In the south pavilion of the Painted Hall of Shouchang, the emperor's residence, stood two companies of egret-drummers and wind players; at either end of Ganshan Hall were chambers of bells and chimes — all of them halls for feasting and music.

sentences.zh: 上數游幸諸苑囿，載宮人從后車。

translations.literal: The emperor often toured the gardens and parks, taking palace women in the following chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited the imperial parks, with palace women riding in the chariots behind him.

sentences.zh: 宮內深隱，不聞端門鼓漏聲，置鍾于景陽樓上，應五鼓及三鼓。

translations.literal: The inner palace was deep and secluded, and one could not hear the drum and water-clock signals at the Upright Gate; a bell was placed on Jingyang Tower to answer the fifth and third watches.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace lay deep and hidden, beyond earshot of the drum and water-clock at the Upright Gate; a bell was hung on Jingyang Tower to mark the fifth and third watches.

sentences.zh: 宮人聞鐘聲，早起莊飾。

translations.literal: When the palace women heard the bell, they rose early and dressed themselves carefully.
translations.idiomatic: At the bell the palace women rose early and dressed with care.

sentences.zh: 車駕數幸琅邪城，宮人常從，早發，至湖北埭，雞始鳴，故呼為雞鳴埭。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage often visited Langya city; palace women regularly followed. Setting out early, they reached Hubei dam just as the cock crowed, so it was called Cockcrow Dam.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage often went to Langya city, palace women following as usual. Setting out before dawn, they reached Hubei dam as the cock first crowed, and the place came to be called Cockcrow Dam.

sentences.zh: 韓蘭英

translations.literal: Han Lanying.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lanying.

sentences.zh: 婦人吳郡韓蘭英有文辭，宋孝武時獻中興賦，被賞入宮。

translations.literal: The woman Han Lanying of Wu commandery had literary talent; in the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Song she submitted a "Fu on the Restoration" and, being rewarded, entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lanying of Wu commandery was a woman of literary gifts; under Emperor Xiaowu of Song she presented a "Fu on the Restoration," won praise, and was taken into the palace.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝時用為宮中職僚。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming of Song she was employed as a palace staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Song she served on the palace staff.

sentences.zh: 及武帝以為博士，教六宮書學。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu came to the throne he made her a erudite and had her teach literacy in the Six Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Qi acceded, he appointed her erudite and set her to teach reading and writing throughout the Six Palaces.

sentences.zh: 以其年老多識，呼為韓公云。

translations.literal: Because she was old and greatly knowledgeable, they called her "Master Han."
translations.idiomatic: Because she was old and full of learning, people called her Master Han.

sentences.zh: 文安皇后王寶明

translations.literal: Empress Wen'an Wang Baoming.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen'an Wang Baoming.

sentences.zh: 永元三年，梁武帝定建鄴，迎入宮，后稱制。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongyuan, when Emperor Wu of Liang secured Jiankang, she was welcomed into the palace and the empress exercised regency.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongyuan, after Emperor Wu of Liang took Jiankang, she was brought into the palace and ruled as regent.

sentences.zh: 至禪位，遜居外宮。

translations.literal: When the throne was abdicated, she withdrew to dwell in an outer palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was surrendered, she withdrew to an outer palace.

sentences.zh: 梁天監十一年薨，葬崇安陵，諡曰安后。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianjian of Liang she died, was buried at Chong'an tomb, and was given the posthumous title Empress An.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tianjian of Liang she died, was buried at Chong'an tomb, and received the posthumous title Empress An.

sentences.zh: 祖韶之自有傳。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Shaozhi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Wang Shaozhi has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王妃何婧英

translations.literal: Consort He Jingying of Prince Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Consort He Jingying of Prince Yulin.

sentences.zh: 郁林王何妃諱婧英，廬江灊人，撫軍將軍戢女也。

translations.literal: Consort He of Prince Yulin, personal name Jingying, was a native of Qian in Lujiang and the daughter of General Who Pacifies the Army Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Consort He of Prince Yulin, whose personal name was Jingying, came from Qian in Lujiang commandery and was the daughter of General Who Pacifies the Army He Ji.

sentences.zh: 初將納為南郡王妃，文惠太子嫌戢無男，門孤，不欲與昏。

translations.literal: At first she was to be taken as consort to the Prince of Nanjun; Crown Prince Wen Hui disliked that Ji had no sons and the clan was isolated, and did not wish the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was to marry the Prince of Nanjun, but Crown Prince Wen Hui disliked that He Ji had no sons and the house stood alone, and did not want the match.

sentences.zh: 王儉以南郡王妃，便為將來外戚，唯須高胄，不須強門。

translations.literal: Wang Jian said that the consort of the Prince of Nanjun would become a future empress consort, and one needed only noble birth, not a powerful house.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian argued that a Prince of Nanjun's consort would become empress consort in time, and what mattered was high lineage, not a powerful clan.

sentences.zh: 今何氏蔭華族弱，實允外戚之義。

translations.literal: Now the He clan's standing among the gentry was modest, which truly fit the principle of empress consort kin.
translations.idiomatic: The He's standing among the gentry was modest — exactly what empress consort kin ought to be.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，乃成昏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming the marriage was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming the marriage took place.

sentences.zh: 妃稟性淫亂，南郡王所與無賴人游，妃擇其美者，皆與交歡。

translations.literal: The consort was by nature wanton. The Prince of Nanjun consorted with riffraff; the consort chose the handsome among them and all had liaisons with her.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was wanton by nature. The Prince of Nanjun kept company with low characters; she picked out the handsome among them and took them all to her bed.

sentences.zh: 南郡王侍書人馬澄年少色美，甚為妃悅，常與鬥腕較力，南郡王以為歡笑。

translations.literal: Ma Cheng, a young attendant scribe of the Prince of Nanjun, was youthful and handsome and greatly pleased the consort; they often arm-wrestled and tested strength, which the prince took as entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Cheng, a young attendant scribe in the prince's service, was fair and pleasing to the consort; they often arm-wrestled and tested their strength, which the prince found amusing.

sentences.zh: 澄者本剡縣寒人，嘗于南岸逼略人家女，為秣陵縣所錄，南郡王語縣散遣之。

translations.literal: Cheng was originally a poor man of Shan county; he had once on the south bank forced himself on a commoner's daughter and was arrested by Moling county, but the Prince of Nanjun spoke to the county and had him released.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was a poor man from Shan county who had once on the south bank seized a commoner's daughter; Moling county arrested him, but the Prince of Nanjun interceded and had him freed.

sentences.zh: 澄又逼求姨女為妾，姨不與，澄詣建康令沈徽孚訟之。

translations.literal: Cheng again tried to force his aunt's daughter to become his concubine; the aunt refused, and Cheng went to the magistrate of Jiankang, Shen Huifu, to sue over it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then tried to force his aunt's daughter into his household as a concubine; when the aunt refused, he brought suit before Shen Huifu, magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 徽孚曰：「姨女可為婦，不可為妾。

translations.literal: Huifu said: "An aunt's daughter may become a wife, not a concubine."
translations.idiomatic: Huifu said, "An aunt's daughter may be taken as a wife, not as a concubine."

sentences.zh: 」澄曰：「僕父為給事中，門戶既成，姨家猶是寒賤，政可為妾耳。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "My father is an attendant within the gates; our house is established — the aunt's family is still low and base and may properly be made a concubine."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "My father is an attendant within the gates; our house is established. The aunt's people are still lowborn — fit only to be a concubine."

sentences.zh: 」徽孚訶而遣之。

translations.literal: Huifu rebuked him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Huifu scolded him and dismissed the case.

sentences.zh: 十一年，為皇太孫妃。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year she became consort to the imperial grand heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year she became consort to the imperial grand heir.

sentences.zh: 又有女巫子楊瑉之，亦有美貌，妃尤愛悅之，與同寢處，如伉儷。

translations.literal: There was also Yang Minzhi, son of a witch, who was also handsome; the consort loved and delighted in him above all, sharing bed and dwelling with him like husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yang Minzhi, a witch's son, handsome as well; the consort doted on him above all others and shared bed and board with him like man and wife.

sentences.zh: 及太孫即帝位，為皇后，封后嫡母劉為高昌縣都鄉君，所生母宋為余杭廣昌鄉君。

translations.literal: When the grand heir took the throne she became empress; her stepmother Liu was enfeoffed as lady of the capital township of Gaochang county, and her birth mother Song as lady of Guangchang township in Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand heir became emperor she was made empress; her stepmother Liu was enfeoffed as lady of the capital township of Gaochang county, and her birth mother Song as lady of Guangchang township in Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 後將拜，鏡在床無因墮地。

translations.literal: Shortly before her investiture as empress, a mirror on the bed fell to the floor for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: Just before her investiture, a mirror on the bed fell to the floor without cause.

sentences.zh: 其冬，與太后同日謁太廟。

translations.literal: That winter she and the empress dowager visited the imperial temple on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: That winter she and the empress dowager paid homage at the imperial temple on the same day.

sentences.zh: 楊瑉之為帝所幸，常居中侍。

translations.literal: Yang Minzhi was favored by the emperor and regularly attended in the inner quarters.
